cells.tense: The practice holds steady, and you are open to what each sitting stirs in you.
cells.act: let yourself be drawn before you choose
cells.ask: Rather than picking your next piece of work, pause at the bench and start with whatever has been pulling at you, then work from there.
cells.core:
You sit down to the work and something in you is already open. The repetitions are steady, the feeling underneath them is welcome rather than managed, and you can tell a session that landed from one that didn't. There is a direction in the practice, and part of it is simply what the work brings up while you do it.

Let that pull have a say in what you pick up. Before the next exercise, sit for a moment and notice which part of the work is reaching for you, then begin there. Anything decided too fast gets filed and forgotten, and a practice only stays alive if something in it is still moving. Nothing here needs acting on. You just let the draw lead, and work from what it brings.
cells.sheetLine: Something in the work is pulling, and you can follow it.
cells.verb: opening to feel what the work brings up
cells.place: alone at the bench with the practice

cells.tense: You are braced for where the practice is heading, so the sitting right here keeps getting short-changed.
cells.act: complete the form so it stands without you
cells.ask: Bring one exercise you have already shaped all the way to its finished form, then set it down, without adding the next stage you had planned.
cells.core:
The practice has gone bright with where it is heading. You can see the finished version, and today's sitting keeps getting measured against that picture and found lacking. The planning runs past the repetitions, and the sessions grow heavier with what they are supposed to become. The openness is real; it is just reaching out beyond what the work can do in this hour.

Bring a piece to the point where it stands finished, then stop. No adding the next stage, no carrying it further because the vision says to. Finishing something at its own size is how you choose from what is actually on the bench instead of from what pulls at you from ahead. Leave it standing there, finished, and start the following session clean.

cells.tense: You kept up the routine after the thing that first opened you had passed.
cells.act: carry what the spark became to its full size
cells.ask: Take up a piece of the practice you began and set aside half-made, and carry it to its end, however small, then set it down.
cells.core:
The repetitions still happen, but the openness that started them has closed. You show up and your hands go through the motions, and nothing in the work feels available or new. What used to open you is now a routine you stand outside of, watching the body do what it has practiced. The practice is running on, and you are somewhere behind it.

Carry something through. Not the whole practice, a piece you began and left when the feeling went out of it. Bring that piece to its end, whatever size it comes out, and set it down done. A finished thing leaves room on the bench for something else to come in, and carrying something the rest of the way, even a little one, is a way of being at the bench again.

cells.tense: The openness in the work is being credited to the routine instead of to you.
cells.act: let the exchange with someone run both ways
cells.ask: In a conversation about your practice, say what you put into it, and let one thing the other person offers simply be received, with nothing paid back on the spot.
cells.core:
You practise alone, and the openness in the work is yours. You are the one who turns up, notices what the session brings up, and keeps the light on. When it comes up in conversation, the credit drifts to the method, the schedule, the habit, as if the openness belonged to the routine and not to the one keeping it. The room can see it. Your own account leaves it out.

The practice was an exchange even alone, and it can run both ways with someone. Say what you give to it, and let one thing that comes back land as received rather than repaid on the spot. The balance does not have to settle before the next breath. What opens in you belongs to you, and saying so is what keeps it yours.
cells.sheetLine: The openness is yours, and the credit keeps drifting elsewhere.
cells.verb: opening to feel what the work brings up
cells.place: alone at the bench with the practice
